hook: SCP-6630 begins as a predator that disguises itself as an ordinary fire, but most of the article is a set of classified files about Henrietta Boone, an engineer who survived its breach. Expect heavy profanity, people burning alive over hours, and sustained psychological cruelty, including threats against a family. The page also offers an accessibility version with the same content.
whyItMatters: It carries the fire-suppression-dept and departmentcon2022 tags, and the department in its containment section is one created in response to the breach. The anomaly section is short and precise; the real weight comes from what happens to one survivor afterward. It is a psychological horror story in which the files themselves, with their reports and responses, become the narrator.
thingsToNotice:
The fire's method, luring rescuers with the screams of a victim it keeps conscious for hours, sets up Boone's own story. Her therapy outbursts add what the official text leaves out: it burns underwater, can melt a bullet in flight, and cannot coexist with real fire, so the only mercy is to set the victim alight.

When she resigns, the report-and-response entries answer with escalating benefits and then Stimulus Protocols: 119 engineering applications rejected plus dozens more in consulting, labor and retail, her sister's medical coverage cancelled, her bank account emptied by a cheerful operator who insists the money was never hers. Even the line that the economy is in terrible shape recurs through her friend, her sister and the operator. In the snowstorm, a man whose name is purged explains the White and Black Playbooks, says she is only on chapter 3, threatens her mother, her brother-in-law and a niece she does not know is coming, and vanishes without leaving a mark on the bench.

She returns, is given a big project, and twenty years later grips O5-10's hand at the Argonaut array, begging to be fired; the Overseer only asks whether she truly believes they can do that. Surveillance is renewed for another twenty years, and the final note mirrors her early nightmares: in 1999 she screamed at the bedroom door that she would not let them in, and in 2022 she sits with her back to it, telling someone unseen to shut up and calling them lucky bastards.
